gaps_for_demo.gap: 10 of the 13 sidebar links are 404s. MAIN_NAV hrefs /inquiries, /buyers, /samples, /quotes, /orders, /payments, /catalog, /documents, /reports, /audit have no page.tsx under src/app/(dashboard)/ (only /, /users, /settings, /access-denied, /account-inactive exist). The owner sees all 13 entries (sidebar.tsx:47 filters by profile.modules; seed gives owner all 13 at seed.sql:54) and clicking any of the 10 shows Next.js's default English 404 page.

No pipeline tables at all: there is no inquiries, samples, quotations, quotation_items, orders, order_items, dispatches, payments or follow_ups table. Migrations stop at catalog+buyers (13 public tables in pg_tables). Nothing to show for Inquiry -> Sample -> Quote -> Order -> Dispatch -> Payment.

Seed auth.users passwords are placeholders, not bcrypt hashes. '$2a$10$abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEF' is 39 characters; a real bcrypt hash is 60 (7-char prefix + 22-char salt + 31-char digest). DB confirms length 39 for all 4 demo users. GoTrue will reject every password. The login page hard-codes 'DemoPass123!' which matches nothing. Also the seed writes only 7 columns and no auth.identities row; GoTrue needs aud/role/instance_id and an identities row for email login.

Login cannot work in the current environment regardless of hashes: the app talks only to Supabase HTTP (GoTrue+PostgREST) at NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321 (login/page.tsx:25 signInWithPassword; server.ts:7-9 createServerClient). Nothing listens on 54321, no Supabase images/volumes exist on this machine, no supabase/config.toml. The Postgres container on 5432 (used by seed/tests) is never touched by the app (no `pg` import in src/). On top of that the .env.local anon/service keys are 51/59-char 'eyJ...' fragments, not 3-segment JWTs, so even a running Supabase would answer 'Invalid API key'.

Migration 0001 cannot run on a fresh plain Postgres: it creates schema auth and auth.uid() but never creates auth.users, yet profiles references auth.users(id). Verified on a fresh database: fails at line 59 with 'relation "auth.users" does not exist' after creating only organizations. The existing container only works because someone hand-created a 7-column auth.users shim that is in no repo file.

No session refresh: there is no src/middleware.ts and server.ts swallows cookie writes inside Server Components (try/catch at 15-29). After the access token expires (Supabase default 1 hour) every RSC render re-refreshes without persisting; with refresh-token rotation the demo user gets kicked to /login mid-demo.

Home page is a tech status board, not a work screen: 'Postgres RLS Active', 'Tenant ID', 'fn_current_org()', module registry with Granted/Locked badges. No business numbers (open inquiries, quotes waiting, orders in production, money due) and no 'today's follow-ups'.

Seed has zero pipeline data, so every new list screen will open empty in the demo. Need 8-10 inquiries across statuses, 3 samples, 4 quotes (1 accepted), 3 orders (1 in production, 1 dispatched, 1 delivered), 1 dispatch with INV/SDN numbers, 3 payments (one partial, one overdue), follow-ups due today. Seed is also not re-runnable for price_list_items/product_costs/buyer_contacts (no ON CONFLICT).
No way to give the buyer a paper: no quotation/PI/invoice print view, no PDF, no WhatsApp share link. For this client 'send bhav on WhatsApp' and 'print bill' are the two things they will ask to see.
gaps_for_demo.where: (missing) src/app/(dashboard)/quotes/[id]/print, src/app/(dashboard)/orders/[id]/print; app_settings.auto_generate_sdn hint at supabase/seed.sql:154 has no implementation

gaps_for_demo.gap: Layout is desktop-only: fixed 256px sidebar (w-64 fixed left-0) and content offset ml-64. On a 360px phone the sidebar covers 71% of the width and pushes content off screen; no hamburger, no bottom nav, header is h-16 with px-6.
Buyers exist in the DB (4 seeded, with contacts) but have no screen; /buyers 404s. The inquiry and quote forms need a buyer picker and a 'new buyer: name + phone' shortcut.
No products screen even read-only; quote form needs a product picker with default rate from price_list_items (and floor_price guard). /catalog 404s.

`npm run lint` blocks forever: no .eslintrc / eslint.config and no eslint-config-next in devDependencies, so `next lint` opens an interactive 'How would you like to configure ESLint?' prompt (verified). The crm-developer and crm-qa agent rules require `npm run lint`, so every agent run will hang on it.

Row types for pipeline entities, PackagingType, PriceListItem, BuyerContact are missing; StatusBadge/BottomNav/ListCard components do not exist; LABELS has no inquiries/quotes/orders/payments sections.

Users screen: clicking the module label text toggles twice (label onClick plus the synthetic click on the nested checkbox bubbling back to the label), so taps on the text likely do nothing; errors use window.alert(); module chips show raw keys like 'leads','quotes'. Server actions throw Error(...) whose message Next.js masks in production builds, so the UI would show a generic message in prod.

Vitest fixtures leak: afterAll deletes org/profile rows but not the auth.users rows it inserted (3 stale tenant-a/b users confirmed in the container). Harmless for demo, noisy for seed/users list if someone later joins on auth.users.

security_notes.file_ref: supabase/migrations/0001_core_system.sql:354-355 (profiles_tenant_policy FOR ALL) + :29 (GRANT ALL ON ALL TABLES TO authenticated)
security_notes.issue: Privilege escalation by any user: the profiles policy allows UPDATE of any row in the org, including the caller's own role and modules. VERIFIED in the running DB as the sales user: UPDATE profiles SET role='owner', modules=<all 13> WHERE id='<me>' succeeded (UPDATE 1); afterwards product_costs returned 6 rows and fn_require_module('payments') returned true. Reachable from the browser with the anon key + session via PostgREST PATCH /rest/v1/profiles. All three walls fall at once.
security_notes.fix: REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON profiles FROM authenticated; keep SELECT policy org_id = fn_current_org(); add SECURITY DEFINER fn_set_user_access(p_user uuid, p_role text, p_modules text[]) and fn_set_user_active(p_user uuid, p_active boolean) that call fn_require_module('users'), refuse p_user = auth.uid() for role/modules, refuse removing/deactivating the last owner, and require caller role='owner' to grant 'owner'. Rewrite users/actions.ts to call these via rpc. Add a Vitest that the self-escalation UPDATE affects 0 rows / raises.

security_notes.issue: RLS bypass through a view: v_product_costs is owned by postgres (superuser locally; bypassrls on Supabase) and has no security_invoker, so queries run with the owner's rights and ignore the product_costs policy. VERIFIED as sales user: SELECT count(*) FROM product_costs = 0 but FROM v_product_costs = 6 (and it would return every org's costs). 'Rule 5' is void. ci-tenant-check.ts:22-28 only inspects pg_tables, so it never sees this.
security_notes.fix: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_product_costs WITH (security_invoker = true) AS ... (PG15+; local is PG17). Apply security_invoker=true to every future view (v_home_kpis, v_order_balances...). Extend scripts/ci-tenant-check.ts to list pg_views in public and fail unless reloptions contains security_invoker=true. Add a test as sales user expecting 0 rows.

security_notes.issue: Cost data leaks through the audit log: product_costs rows are snapshotted into audit_log.new_data/old_data and the SELECT policy lets every org member read them (the comment says 'audit' module but it is not enforced). VERIFIED as sales user: 6 product_costs audit rows readable with raw_onion_rate_per_kg = 98.00. business_settings audit rows likewise expose bank account numbers to everyone.
security_notes.fix: Policy: USING (org_id = fn_current_org() AND fn_has_module('audit')) where fn_has_module is a non-raising boolean helper; drop the audit trigger on product_costs or redact cost columns in fn_audit; hide 'audit' from non-owners in seed/ROLE_PRESETS.

security_notes.file_ref: supabase/migrations/0001_core_system.sql:29-34 (GRANT ALL / ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES to authenticated)
security_notes.issue: TRUNCATE is not subject to RLS and GRANT ALL includes it. VERIFIED as sales user: TRUNCATE audit_log succeeded (42 rows -> 0). The same holds for every business table (buyers, products, price_list_items...): any logged-in user can wipe a table across ALL tenants. Row-level DELETE is correctly blocked (DELETE 0), only TRUNCATE escapes.
security_notes.fix: Replace GRANT ALL with GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES; REVOKE TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public FROM authenticated; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES likewise; on audit_log additionally REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE (fn_audit is SECURITY DEFINER so inserts still work). Add a ci-tenant-check rule that fails if authenticated holds TRUNCATE on any table.

security_notes.file_ref: supabase/migrations/0002_catalog_and_buyers.sql:127-173 and 0001_core_system.sql:361-369 (tenant-only FOR ALL policies on price_list_items, products, packaging_types, buyers, buyer_contacts, business_settings, app_settings)
security_notes.issue: Wall 1 (database) does not exist for table writes: policies check only org_id, never the module. VERIFIED as the operations user (no 'quotes'/'settings' module): UPDATE price_list_items SET floor_price = 1 changed 12 rows and UPDATE business_settings SET bank_details='[]' wiped the bank accounts. Only the Next.js server action checks hasModule, and PostgREST is reachable directly from the browser with the user's session.
security_notes.fix: Add fn_has_module(p_module text) RETURNS boolean (STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, no RAISE) and split policies per table: SELECT USING (org_id = fn_current_org()); INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE USING/WITH CHECK (org_id = fn_current_org() AND fn_has_module('catalog'|'buyers'|'settings')). For money/state tables (quotations, orders, payments) allow writes only through the SECURITY DEFINER functions (REVOKE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from authenticated).

security_notes.issue: Both SECURITY DEFINER guards trust session GUCs that any connection can set. VERIFIED as authenticated: set_config('app.current_org', '<other org>') made fn_current_org() return that org, and set_config('app.override_module_check','true') made fn_require_module('payments') pass for the sales user. Not reachable through PostgREST today (no RPC runs set_config), but any future RPC that forwards user input to set_config, a leaked DATABASE_URL, or a pooled connection with a stale GUC defeats tenant isolation entirely.
security_notes.fix: Remove the overrides; tests already impersonate via SET ROLE authenticated + request.jwt.claim.sub (tests:96-97). If a service-script override is needed, honour it only when current_user is not 'authenticated'/'anon' (e.g. `IF current_user IN ('postgres','service_role') THEN`), and document it.

security_notes.issue: Number generators are SECURITY DEFINER and executable by any authenticated user without a module check; any user can burn QTN/INV/REC sequence numbers (GST invoice numbering must be gap-free) and spam entity_code_counters for their org.
security_notes.fix: REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION fn_next_code(text), fn_next_doc_no(text) FROM authenticated, PUBLIC; call them only from the state-change functions (fn_quote_accept, fn_order_dispatch, fn_payment_record) which do call fn_require_module. Tests then need SET ROLE back to postgres or a wrapper.

security_notes.issue: Overwrites platform-owned functions on Supabase (owner supabase_auth_admin). On hosted/local Supabase this either fails ('must be owner of function') or, if run by a superuser, replaces Supabase's implementation; future Supabase changes to auth.uid() would be silently lost.
security_notes.fix: Create them only when absent (DO block checking pg_proc), ideally inside the new 0000_auth_shim.sql that is a no-op on Supabase.

security_notes.issue: Cookie set/remove errors are swallowed in Server Components and no middleware refreshes the session, so a refreshed access token is never written back; with Supabase refresh-token rotation this leads to forced logouts and, in edge cases, reuse-detection revoking the whole session family. Uses the deprecated get/set/remove shape although @supabase/ssr 0.5.2 provides getAll/setAll.
security_notes.fix: Add src/middleware.ts implementing the Supabase updateSession pattern (createServerClient with getAll/setAll on request+response cookies, call auth.getUser()), matcher excluding _next/static and images; switch server.ts to getAll/setAll.

security_notes.issue: Service-role client exists (unused today). If a developer imports it in a page or action it silently bypasses RLS for the whole request path; nothing prevents importing it from a client component except convention.
security_notes.fix: Add `import 'server-only'` at the top, keep it out of src/app/(dashboard)/** (lint rule no-restricted-imports), use it only in scripts/seed-users.ts for auth.admin.createUser.

security_notes.issue: Demo password 'DemoPass123!' and the four demo emails are compiled into the public client bundle and documented. Acceptable for the demo, dangerous when the same template is deployed for a real client.
security_notes.fix: Render the 'Try as' buttons only when NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_MODE === 'true'; rotate/remove seed users for client deployments; keep this in the project template checklist.

security_notes.issue: Any holder of the 'users' module (not only owners) can set anyone's role to owner, strip the last owner, or change their own modules through the action; toggleUserStatus only blocks deactivating yourself, not the last owner. Also errors are thrown as Error whose messages Next.js masks in production.
security_notes.fix: Move the rules into fn_set_user_access/fn_set_user_active (see critical finding 1) and return {ok:false, message} from actions instead of throwing.

security_notes.issue: fn_audit stores full row JSON, so business_settings audit rows contain complete bank account numbers and IFSC/SWIFT; combined with the open audit_log SELECT policy every staff member can read them.
security_notes.fix: Gate audit_log by 'audit' module (owner only) and strip bank_details from the audit payload for business_settings (jsonb - 'bank_details').

security_notes.issue: Checked explicitly for the task: every FOR ALL policy does carry a matching WITH CHECK (org_id = fn_current_org()); audit_log is SELECT-only by design. No missing WITH CHECK found. The gap is module scoping (see high finding), not tenant scoping. Cross-tenant read/update/delete are blocked (tests 94-132 pass).
security_notes.fix: Keep the pattern; add the module condition to write policies as described.

security_notes.issue: The CI check validates tables only; it cannot catch views without security_invoker, TRUNCATE grants, SECURITY DEFINER functions executable by authenticated, or policies lacking a module condition on write. It passed while the view bypass and TRUNCATE issues existed.
security_notes.fix: Extend with: pg_views must have security_invoker=true; information_schema.role_table_grants must not grant TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER to authenticated; list SECURITY DEFINER functions and require an allowlist.

risks: The app is wired for Supabase Auth (GoTrue + PostgREST) but every script and test was built against a plain Postgres 17 container with a hand-made auth.users shim; nobody has ever logged into this app. The first 'supabase start' + seed may surface more incompatibilities (0001's CREATE OR REPLACE auth.uid() ownership error, GRANT ALL on Supabase-managed roles, seed users without identities). Budget half a day for step 3 before any module work.

First `npx supabase start` pulls ~1.5-2 GB of images; on a slow link this blocks QA and both developers who need a login. Mitigation: step 3 developer starts it immediately, in parallel with designers.

Three developers in parallel share the schema story: dev-2's 'Buyer accepted' button depends on dev-3's fn_quote_accept and dev-3's orders FK depends on dev-2's quotations table. docs/design/contracts.md (step 5) must pin table names, status words and function signatures before step 8-10 start; migrations are numbered 0004/0005/0006 so order is fixed.

labels.ts is a hot shared file. Only step 5 (dev-1) edits it; module developers must add their copy in their own module folder (e.g. src/app/(dashboard)/quotes/labels.ts) or the three branches will conflict.
Security fixes (step 4) change the profiles write path; users/actions.ts must be switched to RPC at the same time or the Staff screen breaks. Both are owned by dev-1 to avoid a split.
The seed must become re-runnable (ON CONFLICT everywhere) or every QA 'db reset' doubles price rows and contacts; today three inserts are not idempotent.

Users are not highly educated and speak Gujarati/Hindi; the demo stays English. Plain words plus icons/colours mitigate, but the client may still ask for Gujarati labels; LABELS being the single source keeps that a later, cheap step.
Home KPIs (dev-1, step 5) read v_home_kpis that dev-3 creates in step 10; the Home page must render zeros when the view is missing (try/catch) or the step 6 QA gate fails for the wrong reason.
Print/WhatsApp share is browser print-to-PDF and a wa.me text link, not a server PDF; good enough for the demo but set expectations with the client (no automatic PDF attachment).
Node 24 with Next 14.2.20 and vitest 2 works today (typecheck 0 errors, 5/5 tests) but `next lint` is deprecated territory; pin eslint 8 + eslint-config-next 14.

I left the onion-crm-postgres container running (restart policy unless-stopped) so later steps can use it; it occupies host port 5432, which does not clash with Supabase local (54321/54322) but will clash with any other local Postgres.

fn_current_fy() is declared IMMUTABLE yet defaults to CURRENT_DATE; harmless now, but document numbers generated near 31 March / 1 April could use a cached FY in long-lived prepared statements. Mark it STABLE in the fixes migration.

Demo content realism: buyers and products are strong, but inquiry/quote/order seed rows must use believable Mahuva numbers (₹185/kg white flakes, USD 2250/MT FOB Mundra, 25 kg bags, 10-20 MT lots) or the owner will not trust the screen; designers should hand developers the sample data table.
